articleTitle: Smile with Angry Birds: Two Smile-Interface Implementations
abstract: This paper proposes two implementations for promoting mental well-being in Angry Birds, one of the most popular mobile games. In the first implementation, fog is introduced for hiding some parts of the game stage, and the player must smile in order to erase fog. In the second implementation, a special TNT is introduced, which can be exploded by the player's smile. We evaluate each of the two implementations by analyzing effects on the player's mental status and game satisfaction.

articleTitle: Pet Face Detection
abstract: The technology of human face recognition is very useful and important for man-machine communication and security. Then, many methods of face recognition have been developed and are used for a lot of systems such as digital camera, bank ATM (Automated Teller Machine), home security and so on. These days, most of human faces are precisely recognized with Haar-like features and AdaBoost classifiers. On the other hand, many people have pets such as dogs and cats, and they are friends or even family members for human beings. Then, surveillance cameras have been developed and used for monitoring pets, who are in houses while the owners are away from home. However, the recognition of pet faces is very difficult since there are a variety of patterns on the face. It is not sure that pet faces can be recognized with the same methods as the faces of human beings. Therefore, we have investigated the methods to detect pet faces, especially for cats and dogs. We have used Haar-like and HOG (Histogram of Oriented Gradients) features to construct the classifiers of pet faces. In addition, we have tried to investigate which is better for the pet face detection to use either whole face or parts of the face such as eyes and nose. Finally, we have applied our method to some pictures of cats and dogs, and confirmed that the classifiers have been able to detect the pet faces correctly.

articleTitle: A Privacy-Aware Exergame Platform for Multi-domain Cognitive Training
abstract: Brain training games and aerobic exercises showed promise to improve cognitive ability in past researches, but the effectiveness of cognitive training still remains controversial. To study the effects of different kinds of cognitive interventions, we designed a series of brain training exergames for elders. Different from traditional video games, a projector is used in this system and all the gameplay is showed on the wall. Players need to simultaneously solve the cognitive training problems show on the wall and do some physical actions to choose the answer. Unlike other similar platforms, a laser scanner instead of camera is used in this system to protect the privacy of players.

articleTitle: The Development of a Virtual Doll Companion for Haptic Interaction
abstract: The main purpose of virtual reality is to immerse a user in a virtual environment. However, the most common criticism of the commodity VR controllers is that they are not able to provide effective tactile feedback. In this paper, we propose a 9-DOF sensor driven haptic feedback companion which is here to bridge the virtual and physical worlds. A 9-DoF sensor through UDP protocol allows us to display the doll's position in real-time. Touch sensor enabled servo motor gives users the effective haptic feedback. When the doll shows different facial expressions in the virtual scenarios, the physical head will have different kinds of rotations in real-time.

articleTitle: VR Ikebana Training Simulation for Promoting the Art
abstract: Ikebana is one of the representatives of Japanese traditional culture. This paper develops VR Ikebana training simulation to promote the art of Ikebana among young people. Easy manipulation with VR devices is developed and investigated. To evaluate aesthetically pleasing shapes of Ikebana works in the simulation such as leaves and stems are regarded as geometric shapes, points, lines, and surfaces, and the balance in the layout is statistically quantified.

Author Keywords: ikebana simulation, virtual space, vr device, 3D manipulation

articleTitle: Detection of Characters and their Boundary from Images of Modern Japanese Official Documents Using Fully CNN-based Filter
abstract: An automatic decipherment system for modern Japanese official documents has been developed in this research project in which a method for detecting characters and their boundary using a Fully CNN-based filter is initiated. The accuracy of detecting a boundary was observed to be more than 97% in our experiment.

articleTitle: Information Visualization for Virtual Martial Arts Training
abstract: In martial arts training, it is important to have a training partner; however, this can be difficult due to scheduling problems. This paper proposes information visualization during sparring training in virtual environments. By reproducing offensive moves in the virtual environment, the person practicing understands them stereoscopically and can practice repeatedly without requiring an actual sparring partner. In addition, to improve movement, information about offensive and defensive postures is displayed.

articleTitle: Development of Handwritten Japanese Character Dataset for Auto-Transcription of Modern Japanese Official Documents
abstract: This paper aims at developing a method for creating and correcting a handwritten character dataset for automatic transcription of modern Japanese official documents. The dataset can contain transcription data, images of documents, and handwritten character data. Furthermore, the proposed character database system can verify the data and reduce artificial mistakes. Users can retrieve character images and various other data by employing the proposed system.

articleTitle: Annotation Assistance Using Japanese Sign Language Words Recognition
abstract: This paper describes one of the assistant methods for annotation tasks using Japanese sign language words recognition. The proposed words recognition is composed of body parts tracking, feature extraction, and words recognition. The recognition segments a video into meaningful units and annotates word labels to them automatically. This paper reports evaluation results using a video database for the correctness of words recognition and the work-reduction ratio of annotation tasks.

articleTitle: Interactive Edge-Aware Segmentation of Character Illustrations for Articulated 2D Animations
abstract: Fascinating articulated animations can be created from character illustrations using commercial tools such as Live2D or spine. However, to compose articulated deformable models, artists have to draw each body part separately or segment input illustrations into several body parts manually. In this paper, we present an efficient technique for the segmentation of character illustrations with simple user interactions. The user first draws strokes (i.e., scribbles) on an input illustration to roughly specify body parts, and then the system segments the input character accordingly. Unlike an existing method for this interactive segmentation, our method has the following three advantages. First, our method recognizes weak colored edges as body-part boundaries, which can be missed by the existing method. Second, it lets the user directly specify body-part boundaries around articulations, which are not necessarily image edges and thus often missed by the existing method. Third, our method automatically enlarges body parts around articulations so that adjacent body parts have some overlaps and the resultant character models can be animated without exhibiting gaps between adjacent body parts. We demonstrate that the proposed system enables more efficient segmentation of character illustrations than the conventional technique.

articleTitle: Magical Projector: Virtual Object Sharing Method among Multiple Users in a Mixed Reality Space
abstract: This paper proposes a method to convey virtual objects to other users and share them for enabling collaborative game in a mixed reality space. The use of mixed reality has gained prominence for collaborative game with multiple people in recent years, it, however, is difficult to grasp users each other's operations. In addition, it is difficult to instruct specific virtual objects to the opponents. These problems arise from the collaboration using mixed reality contents through head mount displays and tablet-type devices; These devices can not present the virtual objects coherently because the devices do not recognize the common coordinates, hence it prevents to share the virtual objects. Our proposed method intends to solve the problem by projecting a pointer to the real space using a handy projector. The projected pointer can be used as a clue for establishing the common coordinates. As an example of the method, we implemented a system that can overlaid arbitrary virtual objects at the intended positions and manipulate them using gestures by using projected pointers as markers for mixed reality using head mount display.

articleTitle: Validation of Deep Features Using the 1-NN Algorithm for Image Similarity Computation
abstract: This paper describes a study that examines deep features by using the 1-NN algorithm in image similarity computation. This work extends our previous work that compared a number of deep-feature-extraction techniques, or feature vectors, in image-style classification. Our finding here is that the feature vector where each element is the cosine similarity between respective pair of the VGG-19 conv5_1 layer's feature maps is the most promising for computation of ukiyo-e similarity.

articleTitle: Determining the Appropriate Number of Observers in Eye-Tracking Based Video Saliency Computation
abstract: This paper proposes a new method for suggesting the appropriate number of observers needed in eye-tracking experiments for a given video. We first use the fixation consistency computed as the Similarity between different observers' fixation maps with the ground truth as a feature vector to classify sample video clips into four types. Then these videos are labeled and used to train a support vector machine (SVM) for identifying the class of a given video clip.

articleTitle: Control of Enemies' Behaviors according to the Player's Field of View in VR Games
abstract: Recently, wide viewing angle games using the VR system are increasing. In this research, we divided the wide viewing angle game screen into three areas: response area, recognition area and peripheral area based on previous research. Then we proposed a system that controls enemy characters and stage changes in each area.

articleTitle: Lanterns Lighitng Up by Sound: Visualization of the Sound Space by Colors
abstract: Lanterns Lighting up by Sound is an interactive visualization art which visualizes the distribution of sounds by colors of light. Our work constituted by multiple lanterns and they hang from the ceiling. All lanterns excute by the sound and works as following. Each lantern lights up depending on the volume of sound of it's own position. When a lantern lights up, color of light shows the volume of sound and elapsed time. For example, a lantern detects larger sound, it lights up in warmer color. Then the light of lantern gradually fades out and finally disappears. Collection of lanterns's lights shows the distribution of sound by color, therefore audiences can perceive sound by color. Audiences can interact with this interactive visualization art by making sounds.

articleTitle: Slide Control Device Oriented to Virtual Physics Based Mixed Reality
abstract: We present a wireless slide control device that uses a ultrasonic motor for actuation and that can change the angular velocity when it rotates on a flat table. Since the vibration of the motor is subtle visually and audibly, the device can be used for MR applications in which a virtual friction is to be set.

articleTitle: Preliminary Study to Quantify the Shape Change of the Pole in Pole Vaulting - Detection of the Pole from Video
abstract: In pole vaulting, how vaulter bends a pole strongly and shift it to jumping power is an important technical factor. To clarify their process, we are trying to describe the shape change of pole three-dimensionally. This time, as the first step, we propose a method to extract the pole region based on machine learning.

articleTitle: Composition and Playback for Minimal Music Using Surround Acoustics
abstract: This paper identifies methods for the perceived localization of sounds that describe realistically improbable patterns for music by using surround acoustics. An example would be the perception of an instrument seemingly moving closer and farther to the listener. However, in our experiment, we could not obtain satisfactory results for various reasons described herein.

articleTitle: A Method of Searching Lithic Cores by Average Linkage Clustering
abstract: Stone tools are the main artifacts facilitating archaeological research of the Paleolithic era. The reassembly of stone tools is pretty meaningful for archaeological and anthropological research. According to the practice of reassembling stone tools, finding lithic cores is the best beginning part of reassembly. Meanwhile, for reassembly of mixed stone tools, the number of lithic cores determines the number of groups. However, several published reassembly methods are still hard to specify lithic cores automatically. Therefore, we propose a method for searching lithic cores automatically. Our method extracts features of stone tool models based on the segmented stone surfaces and geometric characteristics, and processes stone tool models by average group linkage clustering to search lithic core. The experiments conducted indicate that our method can find lithic cores successfully among mixed stone tool models.

articleTitle: Interactive Soundscape System Utilising the Automobile
abstract: This study develops a method for interactive soundscape using a car. The soundscape is a compound word that is a combination of "sound" and "landscape." The soundscape is an activity which attempts to understand the cultural and social environment from the nature of sounds or artificial sounds or both. The interactive soundscape composes auditory events by the Global Positioning System and movement of the vehicle. The sound that is presented through the car audio system represents the landscape which is shown outside of the vehicle. For instance, when the automobile is reaching a suburban area, the interactive soundscape system displays sounds of birds or insects or both. Moreover, the sound of an automobile motor is turned into an engine from a classic car that changes, depending on the speed of the vehicle when in the vicinity of an automobile museum. Experiments were done on 6-km roads including suburban and urban areas. Ten landmarks were selected in the test area. Different audio events were set on each marker. Six subjects participated in the test drive. The interactive soundscape was given some input by the participants, such as improvements, including the future of development. The scenery presentation with the sound makes an outdoor environment in the vehicle. This experience has changed the drive to explore.

articleTitle: Graph-Based User Interface for Digest Video Creation Focusing on Specific Persons
abstract: We have been developing a new method to generate digest videos focusing on specific persons appearing in the video. This method generates a user interface for shot selection. We suppose to manually select shots on the user interface and then combine them with automatically selected shots to generate a digest video. As a result, we can insert the shots in which the target is not automatically detected as part of the digest videos, and generate highly satisfied digest videos. This paper presents a new user interface which assists the manual selection of preferable shots. This method aims to collect attractive scenes of specific persons such as actors or musicians.

articleTitle: Development of Communication Tools for Informed Consent Using VR Technology
abstract: Since prostate cancer patients tend to be elderly, doctors may need more time to explain a consent to them, so that they may understand it and sign it. The most direct way to help facilitate this communication is through visualization, specifically using VR tools to describe visually to the patients their prostate, their medical condition as well as the necessary surgical procedures. Our goal is to provide a visualization technology tool which makes medically-related communication between doctors and patients easy and efficient.

articleTitle: Development of Educational Contents for Electronic Circuit Learning - Simple Model Assembly Kit
abstract: Our research is developing an educational content for electronic circuit learning. This paper proposes our content using a simple model assembly kit. This research aims to be a kit that can simulate experiential manufacturing and learning of electronic circuits.

articleTitle: A Possibility of Navigating Users by GVS
abstract: Galvanic vestibular stimulation enables us to control the sense of human balance. We are trying to apply it to outdoor route navigation and established a way to stimulate the subjects sitting down through our indoor experiments. Prior to the outdoor experiments, we have tried to stimulate three subjects standing up in order to find the possibility of applying it to the navigation.

articleTitle: Animated KUI
abstract: We have proposed Kage User Interface(KUI) which uses the real shadow of real world as interface. In this poster, we propose "Animated KUI" as an example of utilization of KUI. Animated KUI manipulates shadow animation by the shadow as an interface. This manipulation can play, stop, play backward the shadow animation by swipe gestures based on touch screen.

articleTitle: Physical Simulation of Baton Rolling on Circular Cylinders
abstract: We present simulation results of rolling a baton on a series of circular cylinders. Realistic materials such as PVC sheets for the cylinders and wood or silicon rubber for the baton are used to find physical parameters with which the baton rolls over the cylinders. We found sets of feasible parameters of frictions and initial forces given to the baton.

articleTitle: Modeling of Olympic Medals Based on Point Cloud Data: Registration between Two Sides of the Same Medal
abstract: In modeling Olympic medals, two sides of the same medal are digitized separately with high resolution 3D scanner because the information punched on its surfaces is important. It needs the post-process of directional registration between independent scanned data sets for each side. This paper presents a method to realize it based on the point cloud feature such as the center of gravity and the principal axis.

articleTitle: A Study of Finding Target Objects for Visualizing Stone Tool Assembly
abstract: In archaeology, joining material is one of the most important pieces of evidence that can be found. Joining materials are generally created by assembling stone tools which are excavated from same ruins. Archaeologists go through trial and error in trying to create and map the structure of the joining materials. Since the joining and assembly in archaeology requires time consuming work, in order to simplify the process, some method using computers is required. Using the assembly instruction of a joining material, it is able to reduce the burden. This paper studies a method of finding target objects to visualize pair of joining materials to a user. Through our method, by using real objects, it allows the assembly of stone tools to be efficient and precise.

articleTitle: Automatic Music Component Selection Based on Impression of Input Movies
abstract: Recently, many people enjoy accompanying background music to movies before uploading them onto social networking services. Many applications and services which assist the background music editing have been released. However, it is still often bothering and time-consuming to select and edit the background music. This paper presents a technique to automatically select music components to generate the background music that matches impression of movies.

articleTitle: A Case Study on Sound Design Analysis of Romantic Audio Drama for Female Applied the Theory of Cinema Audio
abstract: In this case study, we attempt to analyze POV shot style audio drama to explorer the elements and functions which influence the sense of "point of audition" and "for-me-ness." Timeline and function analysis of audio drama of less than 6 hours total was carried out referring to B of A with "clarity/fidelity," "foreground/background" "diegetic/non-diegetic," as a parameter. Timeline and function analysis of audio drama of less than 6 hours total was carried out referring to "5 binaries" of D. Neumeyer with "clarity/fidelity," "foreground/background" "diegetic/non-diegetic," as a parameter. Especially for clarity/fidelity, unlike cinema audio practice, it was suggested that fidelity is also used to increase "for-me-ness".

Author Keywords: Sound Design, Cinema Audio, Audio Drama, Point of Audition, for-me-ness

articleTitle: A Semi-automatic Technique for Selection of Well-Balanced Photo Sets
abstract: Recently, everyone can easily take photos and retain. But people need time and labor to organize and share photo data if they have too many. In this paper, we present a method for automatically selecting a balanced set of photos from many photo data by selecting same extends photos with different feature values. Also, we provide a user interface that shows the result of choosing photos.

Author Keywords: Photo selection, Graph coloring, Image feature

articleTitle: Interactive Texture Chooser Using Interactive Evolutionary Computation and Similarity Search
abstract: This paper presents an interactive texture chooser. This interactive texture chooser allows novice users to obtain their desired textures by checking each 3D model that mapped the texture. Current 3D computer graphics (3DCG) software products provide a convenient means of dealing with 3D content for novice users. Textures are frequently used in several 3DCG tools. Users may use certain tag and categorical search interfaces for texture choices when they decide on each texture for a 3D mapping task. However, making textures choices can be challenging for novices because they have no sufficient knowledge about 3DCG. There are various types of textures even if several textures are classified in the same category. For example, searching for the desired stone texture can be challenging from the stone texture category because hundreds of textures have the same tag and are classified under the same category. In addition, the tag and categorical search interfaces are no longer available when a user does not have a specific target in his/her mind. The proposed interactive texture chooser solves the above issues. This system consists of an interactive evolutionary computation (IEC) mode and a similarity search (SS) mode. The IEC mode displays some texture candidates using an evolutionary computation algorithm. The SS mode consists of a visual similarity search function based on several texture features. The effectiveness of this system has been confirmed through experimental results.

articleTitle: Development of Analytical Method on Musical Effect Sound in Japanimation Works
abstract: The purpose of this research is developing to analyze method and re-production technique of musical sound effects given to a specific scene in Japanimation, especially expressing feelings and circumstances such as anxiety, restlessness, fear, tension, thought of anime characters. We planned our research method that consists on 2 elements. The first one is musicology, especially musical analysis and reproducing method. The second one is cinema audio analysis theories established by M. Chion, D. Neymeyer, D. Sonnenschein etc. An investigation the Japanimation's musical effects were conducted using transcription method in musicology. As a result of the analysis, synthesized sounds were used in 76 out of 83 scenes were used regardless of pitched or unpitched, and the sound classified as "Pitched, mono voice" was the most frequent. Based on this result, a reproduction experiment using the current DAW system was carried out as an evaluation experiment. Most of sounds were able to reproduced. It was successful most of subjects by DAW.

Author Keywords: Sound Design, Anime, Cinema Audio, Sound Effect
